implementerProof.how: Every entry of implement.json's proof array was re-driven independently in this tester's own role container (a container of the same pod, clean: no node_modules, no /tmp/bunx-*, no /legion/bun before I started) and in a throwaway copy of this tree I made myself at /legion/workspaces/infra-71-test. AC1: re-ran the prescribed commands clean and then poisoned, and reproduced the pre-change form's silent green and its 0.3.3 version answer. AC2: ran .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh on the real tree (exit 0, same counts the implementer quoted: 13 manifests, 8 workflows, 92 shell scripts, 536 guides) and its 53-case suite, and put the vulnerable form back in a fixture of my own rather than in the tree. AC3/AC5: ran the deployment's own setup argv in my copy, cold and warm, and measured the container's own disk across it. AC4: injected all three failures and then drove the notice on the real Oh My Pi binary. Two corrections to what the implementer wrote, neither a defect in the change: its AC3 line says 29.0 s cold, where a truly empty BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR cost 46.9 s here (its 29.0 s run reused /legion/bun/cache from an earlier run of the phase); and its AC1 line's claim that `bunx --no-install biome check .` passes only after the plain form has run is exact — I confirmed the clean container has no /tmp/bunx-<uid>-biome@latest until the plain form creates it.

failures.criterion: AC2 — 'the required lint job fails if the vulnerable form reappears'. It does not: `bun x biome check .` and `npx biome check .` are the same command as `bunx biome check .`, reach the same squatted package and pass the guard everywhere it judges.
failures.evidence: Measured in this role container at the code head bd983cfd, workspace with no node_modules: `bun x biome check .` exits 0 having checked nothing and `bun x biome --version` answers 0.3.3 (bun's own alias for bunx — one binary, one resolution); `npx biome check .` exits 0 and `npx biome --version` answers 0.3.3 too, and the worker image ships /usr/local/bin/npx and /usr/local/bin/npm beside bun. The guard reads only each segment's first word (.github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh:164-185, `offenders`), so `bun` and `npx` are neither `bunx` nor one of the four pinned tool names and nothing is reported. Proven against the guard itself in a fixture built the way its own suite builds one: a tree whose AGENTS.md fenced block holds `bun x biome check .`, `npx biome check .` and `bunx biome check .` is failed for the `bunx` line alone ('AGENTS.md:6: this fenced command runs `bunx`', 1 place(s)); a tree carrying `bun x` in a lint recipe, a workflow `run:`, a shell script line and a fenced block passes with 'every prescribed biome, tsc, tsserver and playwright command runs through scripts/repo-tool.sh'. Red test: the three cases of `case: \`bun x\` and \`npx\` are the same command spelled another way` in .github/scripts/check-check-commands.test.sh, committed at f2f525742ce3; `PYTHONPATH=/legion/pytools .github/scripts/check-check-commands.test.sh` reports 'Results: 53 passed, 6 failed' at that commit, the six failures being those three cases' two assertions each. Neither spelling appears anywhere the guard judges today (`npx` only in docs/research/knowledge-graph-tools/, which is not prescriptive and is no check tool), so the fix breaks nothing in the tree.

proof.criterion: AC1 — in a role container where the repository's packages are not installed, no command the repository tells an agent to run reports a passing lint, including in a container poisoned by a plain `bunx biome`.
proof.surface: This tester's own role container of the issue pod (worker image, bun 1.3.14, uid 1000), $LEGION_WORKSPACE with no node_modules, first clean (no /tmp/bunx-*) and then poisoned by one `bunx biome check .`.
proof.command: bun run lint packages/pi-legion/ ; bun run typecheck ; (cd packages/pi-legion && bun run lint) ; scripts/repo-tool.sh biome check . ; scripts/repo-tool.sh tsc --version — each run twice, before and after `bunx biome check .` poisoned the container
proof.observed: Every one exits 1 with `repo-tool: biome is not installed` or `repo-tool: tsc is not installed`, both paths tried (./node_modules/.bin/<tool> and /legion/workspaces/sjawhar/legion/infra-71/node_modules/.bin/<tool>) and the remedy naming `bun install` and scripts/legion-setup.sh. The poisoning changes nothing: the same five exit 1 with the same message afterwards. No command reports a check it did not run.
proof.negativeControl: The pre-change form in the same container: clean, `bunx biome check .` prints three resolution lines and exits 0 having checked no file, and `bunx biome --version` answers 0.3.3 — the squatted package, not the Biome 2.4.11 bun.lock pins. Once that run has left /tmp/bunx-1000-biome@latest, `bunx --no-install biome check .` also exits 0, the state the spec says the failure needs.

proof.criterion: AC2 (the half that holds) — the guard fails a `bunx` or a bare pinned tool wherever a prescribed command is written, and passes the tree as it stands.
proof.surface: .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh on the real tree, and fixtures of my own built as its suite builds them (the real script symlinked into a miniature repository).
proof.observed: The tree passes: `every prescribed biome, tsc, tsserver and playwright command runs through scripts/repo-tool.sh (13 manifest(s), 8 workflow(s), 92 shell script(s), 536 guide(s))`, exit 0 in 1.8 s. The suite reports `Results: 53 passed, 0 failed` before my red cases. It is wired where it has to be: pr-and-main.yaml:72 runs the guard in the required lint job and pr-and-main.yaml:266 runs the suite in the test job. The guard's guide set misses nested guides (packages/envoy/infra/AGENTS.md, packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md, docs/site/media/broker/README.md and nine more are matched by none of its patterns), but I read all twelve: not one prescribes a biome, tsc, tsserver or playwright command, so nothing escapes it today.
proof.negativeControl: A fixture whose AGENTS.md fenced block holds `bunx biome check .` is failed at the line inside the block (`AGENTS.md:6: this fenced command runs \`bunx\``, `1 place(s)`), exit 1 — with the tree's own files never edited.

proof.criterion: AC3 (pre-merge proxy; the full line is the production check) — the packages are in place, the lint command answers with the version bun.lock pins and its `Checked N files` line, nothing of the install is on the container's own filesystem, and the workspace's tracked files, bun.lock among them, are unchanged by it.
proof.surface: A throwaway copy of this tree I made on the issue volume (/legion/workspaces/infra-71-test, no node_modules), run through the exact argv the deployment's setup line uses, with stdin on /dev/null and stdout redirected onto stderr as the daemon's wrapper does (packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/plugins.go setupBlock), and with BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR set to the issue-volume path the Sandbox runtime gives every role container (manifest.go roleEnvironment).
proof.command: env LEGION_WORKSPACE=/legion/workspaces/infra-71-test LEGION_ISSUE=INFRA-71 LEGION_ROLE=tester LEGION_GENERATION=1 LEGION_STATE_DIR=/legion/test-state BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/legion/scratch/bun/install/cache /bin/sh -c 'if [ -r ./scripts/legion-setup.sh ]; then sh ./scripts/legion-setup.sh; fi' </dev/null 1>&2 ; then ./node_modules/.bin/biome --version ; bun run lint . ; cksum bun.lock ; a cksum manifest of all 4739 non-node_modules files before and after
proof.observed: Exit 0 after `1986 packages installed`, 46.9 s against a truly empty cache. `./node_modules/.bin/biome --version` and `scripts/repo-tool.sh biome --version` both answer `Version: 2.4.11`, the version bun.lock pins, and `bun run lint .` prints `Checked 1079 files in 37s`. `cksum bun.lock` is 581893351 340936 before and after, and the 4739-file manifest is identical across the run. The container's own disk took exactly one empty file, /tmp/.1afc7be39edfdfff-00000000.hm (0 bytes, bun's own temp): $HOME/.bun is 113086919 bytes before and after and $HOME/.cache 10821129 before and after. $LEGION_STATE_DIR holds no report after a successful run, and the marker /legion/bun/state/installed holds the lock's cksum.
proof.negativeControl: In that same copy immediately before the run, `bun run lint .` exits 1 with `repo-tool: biome is not installed`. And a marker left by another workspace of the same volume does not satisfy the guard: a second directory on the volume carrying the same bun.lock and no node_modules installs rather than exiting 'already installed'.

proof.criterion: AC4 (the half that is pre-merge) — a role whose install failed still starts, with what failed in front of its agent in its first turn.
proof.surface: The throwaway copy with each failure injected, and a real Oh My Pi pane: the pinned binary at /opt/omp/bin/omp driven through @legion/pi-shared/test/omp-harness's runLegionPane with this checkout's two plugin entries, a stand-in daemon and listener, and the report written into the pane's own LEGION_STATE_DIR.
proof.command: LEGION_SETUP_INSTALL_TIMEOUT=1 sh scripts/legion-setup.sh ; BUN_CONFIG_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:1/ sh scripts/legion-setup.sh ; /usr/bin/flock on the cache with LEGION_SETUP_LOCK_WAIT=1 ; sh scripts/legion-setup.sh with LEGION_STATE_DIR unset ; sh scripts/legion-setup.sh with LEGION_WORKSPACE unset ; sh scripts/legion-setup.sh in a workspace with no bun.lock ; LEGION_TEST_OMP=/opt/omp/bin/omp bun test extensions/throwaway-setup-notice-omp.test.ts (4 cases, removed afterwards)
proof.observed: Every injection exits 0, leaves no marker, and writes valid JSON to $LEGION_STATE_DIR/legion-setup-report.json carrying this run's issue, role and generation: install-timeout with exitStatus 124; install-failed with exitStatus 1 and a detail bounded at 999 characters; lock-timeout with exitStatus 199 and the line `another install held /legion/scratch/bun/install/cache for more than 1s`. A failure with LEGION_STATE_DIR unset still exits 0 and writes nothing; no LEGION_WORKSPACE and a workspace with no bun.lock are both silent exit 0. On the real binary the pane whose report matches its own issue, role and generation carries, as the very first message of its first provider request, `Legion's setup command could not install this repository's packages in this container: reason "install-timeout", exit status 124`, the log tail, and the `sh scripts/legion-setup.sh` retry advice — with /legion/v1/claims/register among the pane's requests, so the extension had really booted.
proof.negativeControl: Three panes of the same shape whose report is not this agent's news carry no such text: one whose generation is 9, one whose role is reviewer, and one whose report is not JSON — each still registering and running its turn (4 pass, 0 fail). A fourth control caught my own rig: a pane run against a partially installed node_modules loads neither plugin and answers a turn with no notice at all, which is why every case asserts the registration call before it reads the turn.

proof.criterion: AC5 (pre-merge proxy; the two-role form in a pod is the production check) — a second role of the same issue, starting while the packages are already there, installs nothing; and roles starting at the same moment do not corrupt the one node_modules they share.
proof.surface: The throwaway copy: a second run under another role's identity, and then six concurrent runs under the six role names, cold cache and warm, each with a LEGION_STATE_DIR of its own.
proof.command: env LEGION_ROLE=reviewer … sh scripts/legion-setup.sh after a successful run ; then rm -rf node_modules and the marker and start all six at once, once against an empty BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR and once against a warm one
proof.observed: The second role prints `this bun.lock's packages are already installed; nothing to do` in 0.036 s, exit 0; the shared cache is byte-identical across it (1395639291 bytes before and after) and no file under node_modules is newer than the marker. Six at once: every one exits 0 with no report, the whole set finishing in 30 s cold and 14 s warm — one install and five that wait on /usr/bin/flock and then re-run bun install in about a second each — and node_modules/.bin/biome afterwards answers Version: 2.4.11. No ENOENT and no retry line in any of the twelve logs.
proof.negativeControl: Remove node_modules/.bin/biome and run again: the marker alone does not satisfy the guard and the script installs (`1824 packages installed`), which is what makes an interrupted install cost the next role an install rather than a silent skip.

observations: The script's lock wait (90 s) is half its install timeout (180 s), so a first install slower than 90 s leaves every other role of the pod reporting lock-timeout to its agent although the install then succeeds. Self-healing — the notice's own advice re-runs the script, which exits 'already installed' — and unreachable in what I measured (46.9 s cold, 28 s cold under six-way contention), so it is an observation, not a failure.

A failed run removes /legion/bun/state/installed, which is the volume's marker rather than the workspace's: a second workspace on one issue volume whose install fails costs the first workspace's roles a reinstall. Production puts one clone on an issue volume (workspace-init provision), so nothing reaches it today; I met it only because my throwaway copy shared the volume.
LEGION_*, DISPATCH_* and ENVOY_* scrubbing was not part of this issue's acceptance, so no such evidence is recorded here.

packages/pi-legion/extensions/legion-role-tools-omp.test.ts passes against a partially installed node_modules, where neither plugin entry loads: its assertions hold for a pane with no Legion extension at all. Not this change's doing and not in its diff — reported here because it cost me a wrong reading of the notice before I caught it.
